titulo: Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis?
fuentes: deWeber K, Olszewski M, Ortolano R. Knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis. Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine, 2011;24(2):169-174. https://www.jabfm.org/content/24/2/169 (215 respondents aged 50-89; habitual knuckle cracking 'does not seem to be a risk factor for hand OA')
Kawchuk GN et al. Real-Time Visualization of Joint Cavitation. PLOS ONE, 2015. (real-time MRI: a dark void appears in the joint at the time of the sound; authors interpret it as a gas bubble)
destinatario: se lo manda alguien a su amigo que cruje todos los nudillos antes de escribir para decirle que se quede tranquilo
receta: el que lo hace mal (mito del cuerpo) con capa de datos

frases.texto: You've been told that cracking your knuckles gives you arthritis.
frases.estilo: Dry and confident, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Researchers in a 2011 study surveyed over two hundred adults, ages fifty to eighty-nine.
frases.estilo: Matter of fact, setting up the evidence.

frases.texto: People who cracked their knuckles had no more hand arthritis than people who didn't.
So what's the pop? An MRI study filmed it.
A dark gap opens up in the joint as the sound happens. Researchers think it's a bubble of gas.
Heads up: those are small studies, and a perfect one is almost impossible to run.
But so far, the pop alone isn't a reason to panic.
Send this to the friend who cracks every knuckle before typing.
frases.estilo: Playful, with humor, as a punchline.
